1: Paired confusion matrices on the common-complete test cohort. Failures are reported separately in Table 5; rows are reference grades.
10: Correctness and review accounting under fixed development thresholds. Test coverage may differ from 80%; inference failures always enter review. Thresholds were selected without test labels.
11: Paired changes from each model’s own unmodified image results. Bars are 95% provisional prefix-bootstrap intervals on common-complete pairs. Holm-adjusted tests are supplied separately. Transformations are engineering controls, not validated acquisition shifts.
12: Correctness-aware prompt stability by reference grade and all-case accuracy under target, blank and shuffled-image controls. Stable errors are counted separately. Controls use original references and are not pooled with the main cohort; they do not establish causal explanations.
13: Measured quality and runtime. Horizontal and vertical bars are grouped 95% intervals; marker area increases with peak allocated GPU memory. Quality and timing cohorts are separately named in Table 17. No optimal frontier is asserted.
14: Synchronized component means sum to end-to-end warm means. Processing/transfers are shown as an additional component so their cost is not silently assigned to image encoding. Loading, target disk reads and training are separate; support images are reprocessed without prefix caching. Timing hooks add synchronization overhead.
2: Ordinal error distances and grade-specific recall. Recall bars are 95% provisional prefix-bootstrap intervals; rare-grade resamples without support are excluded and counted in Table 6.
3: Prompt and demonstration comparisons. QWK uses each configuration’s complete cases; recall uses their common-complete cohort. Bars are 95% provisional prefix-bootstrap intervals.
4: Three fixed training-only support sets evaluated on the same test targets. Intervals quantify case sampling uncertainty; differences between the three sets are descriptive and do not justify selecting the best test set.
5: Measured downstream label budgets and performance, with grouped 95% intervals. Zero denotes no KL gradient fitting, not absence of foundation pretraining. No scaling law or full-data adapter result is inferred.
6: Paired correctness transitions and grade recall after adaptation, when feasible. Failed or omitted adaptation is stated explicitly and is not replaced by simulated performance.
7: Top-label reliability in 15 fixed equal-width bins; empty bins are omitted, marker area reflects support. Model-level metric intervals appear in Table 11. Scaling does not change the selected grade.
8: Frozen P0 confidence distributions before and after temperature scaling. Correctness is unchanged; reduced confidence alone is not improved grading.
9: Risk versus all-case coverage. Rankings use calibrated confidence; failures are never released. Bars at 60%, 80% and 90% show 95% provisional prefix-bootstrap intervals with ranking recomputed within each resample. Random ordering is a descriptive reference.
